codeReview.area: Core/Analysis — disk detection, virtual detector, calibration (refutation pass)
codeReview.summary: I could not kill any of the four outright — every cited line says substantially what was claimed, and I verified each against the code, the py4DSTEM lock, docs/open-items.md and git history. But I materially weakened three and corrected the severity on three. What is genuinely good here: the code is right in every case — `originFitIsSane` reads the full-scan RMS as Gate B demanded, `judgedOriginResidual` exists precisely so the panel and the verdict cannot drift onto different numbers, the estimator refuses nothing and says so, and `Calibration.swift:533-560` documents the refuted swap in unusual, reproducible detail. Every defect below is prose, a dead parameter, or an underived constant — none of them currently computes a wrong number. Killed outright: 0. Downgraded: finding 1 high→medium (the code is correct and the definitive correction sits 110 lines below the stale line in the same file; the strongest evidence is not the cited line at all but the UI comment), finding 2 medium→low (the file's own comment block already records the threshold cut, and no number changes), finding 4's stated failure narration is wrong for the app's actual path and I rewrote it. Finding 3 stands as written at low.

findings.title: The revert of the S13 robust-residual gate left three prose claims saying the gate still reads `robustResidual` — one of them unambiguous
findings.why: REFUTER NOTE — what I checked, and where the reviewer overstated: I read `Calibration.swift:415-423` in full. The cited sentence is "…comparing *it* to a full-scan threshold would be circular. Measured on `Particle_1…bin8`: 2.19 px here against 18.47 px full-scan… The gate reads this one deliberately — see `originFitIsSane`." "this one" is AMBIGUOUS: the coherent reading of the paragraph's own argument (comparing the robust number to a full-scan threshold is circular) is that the gate reads the full-scan one just named, which is what the code does. `git log -L 415,424` shows the whole block was ADDED by 185d9bb, the very commit that reverted the swap — so it was written post-revert and is probably poorly worded rather than wrong. I therefore moved the finding's anchor. What is NOT ambiguous, added by the same commit (`git log -L 52,56:CalibrationDetailsView.swift`), is `CalibrationDetailsView.swift:52-55`: "the residual the GATE judged, which is the robust one where a robust fit ran. Showing `rmsResidual` here while the verdict came from `robustResidual`…" — `judgedOriginResidual` is `origin?.rmsResidual` (`Calibration.swift:580`) and `originFitIsSane` reads `origin?.rmsResidual` (`Calibration.swift:569-571`), so both sentences are false. Third instance confirmed: `docs/open-items.md:505` (live prose, outside the `~~…~~` strikethrough that ends at :499) asserts "the gate — renamed `originFitIsSane` — reads the **robust** residual", contradicted by the live item at `docs/open-items.md:617`. Severity cut high→medium because the code is correct, `judgedOriginResidual` structurally prevents the panel and the verdict from quoting different numbers, no exported value is mislabelled (`ResultExport.swift:435` writes the neutral key `origin_fit_residual_px`), and any reader who follows the cited pointer to `originFitIsSane` lands on 30 lines (`Calibration.swift:533-560`) that state "**It reads the FULL-SCAN residual**" with Gate B's counterexample. It is a doc-accuracy violation of the repo's "no claim stands that a reader cannot reproduce" rule and a fresh instance of the 2026-08-27 failure mode, not a live science defect.
findings.failureScenario: A session auditing the calibration panel reads `CalibrationDetailsView.swift:52-55`, believes the displayed "Fit residual" is the kept-set residual, and either quotes it to a user as "2.19 px over the 73% of positions used" when it is in fact the full-scan 18.47 px, or concludes `originFitIsSane` has drifted off the intended statistic and "fixes" it to `origin?.robustResidual` — reinstating exactly what Gate B measured (32×32 scan, 12×12 corner thrown +40 px: fit displaced 15.03 px, `keptResidual` 9.94 passes against probe radius 10.624, full-scan 15.64 blocks), after which `originSupportsReciprocalMetrology` passes and Q is calibrated in a 15 px-displaced frame.

findings.title: Seven ellipse-fit refusal thresholds carry no derivation and no DEVIATION note, on a path py4DSTEM does not gate at all
findings.why: REFUTER NOTE — I confirmed the rule violation and rewrote the failure scenario, which the reviewer got wrong. Verified: `grep DEVIATION mac4DSTEM/Core/Analysis/EllipseCalibration.swift` returns NOTHING, while `fit1D` is declared "Port of py4DSTEM `fit_ellipse_1D`'s operative model" (`:70-72`); and `References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/calibration/ellipse.py:28-79` confirms `fit_ellipse_1D` returns whatever `leastsq` gives with no acceptance test of any kind (its only `assert`s, `:173`/`:206`, are shape and p0-length checks in `fit_ellipse_amorphous_ring`). All eight constants are where claimed: `:79`, `:122-123`/`:131`, `:213-215`, `:240-241`, `:496`. The two-statistics-one-name conflation is real: `fit1D`'s residual is `sqrt(Σ[(Adx²+Bdxdy+Cdy²−1)·I]²/ΣI²)` (`:143-152`, `:222`) while `fitAmorphousRing`'s is `sqrt(Σε²/N)/dynamicRange` (`:488-491`), both stored in `normalizedResidual`, documented at `:32` as one "dimensionless residual", and gated at the adjacent 0.2 and 0.22. WHERE THE REVIEWER WAS WRONG, corrected here: the app never uses `fit1D`'s 0.2 default — `AppState.swift:4154-4158` calls only `fitBestAvailable` with defaults, and `fitBestAvailable` passes `maximumResidual: max(0.4, maximumConicResidual)` into `fit1D` (`:249`), so a 0.25 conic is NOT refused there; the app's operative refusals are the 0.22 profile gate (`:241`) and the `conic.conicResidual <= 0.2` fallback re-throw at `:259`. The UI also labels the model immediately above the number (`CalibrationDetailsView.swift:142-148`), which blunts the conflation for a careful reader. Severity kept medium on the silent-acceptance half only. `docs/open-items.md` has no entry for any of this (grepped "ellipse": only :415, :1773, :1925, none about thresholds), so it is not a known item.
findings.failureScenario: Silent-acceptance direction (the one that matters, PLAUSIBLE): a partial ring occupying exactly 12 of 36 angular sectors clears `occupiedCount >= angularBinCount / 3` (`:131`) and a 4:1 conic clears `ellipse.b / ellipse.a >= 0.2` (`:213`), so a near-degenerate ellipse — the case py4DSTEM keeps `constrain_degenerate_ellipse` (`ellipse.py:251`) around for — is stamped `calibrationProvenance.ellipse = .measuredInApp` (`AppState.swift:4163-4165`) and applied to every calibrated Bragg vector, strain map and ACOM orientation with no refusal and no derivation anyone can check. False-refusal direction (visible, so less severe): a broad amorphous halo whose profile residual lands at 0.23 against `maximumProfileResidual = 0.22` (`:241`, `:285`) and whose conic residual exceeds 0.2 has its error re-thrown at `:259`, and the user is told "Detector ellipse fit residual is too large" quoting the PROFILE statistic against a threshold derived from nothing, with a real elliptical distortion left uncorrected.

findings.title: `KnownCrystalQCalibration.estimate` takes `probeRadiusPixels` and never reads it, while its doc promises a check that runs on it
findings.why: REFUTER NOTE — confirmed by reading the whole function body (`QCalibration.swift:114-190`): `probeRadiusPixels` is declared at `:119` and referenced nowhere else in the file; the only `.notSelfChecked` constructions, `:178` and `:180`, both derive from `expectedRatio` i.e. `secondShellRadiusInvAngstrom`. Swift emits no unused-parameter warning, so nothing catches it. The doc at `:105-110` is therefore false for one of the two arguments it names. Verified the parameter is live at four call sites (`AppState.swift:5037,5056`, `tools/real-acom-benchmark/main.swift:101`, `tools/training-dataset-campaign/main.swift:771`, plus `tools/origin-fit-diagnostics/shell-check.swift:154`), which is what sustains the illusion. Severity cut medium→low for two reasons the reviewer did not weigh: the file's OWN 30-line block at `:68-99` explicitly records that `minimumShellRadiusRatioOfProbe = 1.0` was cut by Gate B and that the probe radius is unreliable anyway (2.15× over-measured), so the misleading doc is half self-correcting; and no scientific number changes — the estimator refuses nothing by design (`:111-112`). I also softened one reviewer claim: the harness comment at `tools/q-calibration-gate-test/main.swift:444-445` says "Passing nil for the crystal's second shell must do the same, which is why that argument has no default value" — it attributes the `.notSelfChecked` to the second shell alone, not to both, so it is not itself a false claim; the `probeRadiusPixels: 5` at `:390,425,436` are indeed inert.
findings.failureScenario: A reviewer or session auditing what the Q estimator self-checks reads `QCalibration.swift:106-110` — "a caller that cannot supply them gets an estimate whose checks silently did not run… Pass nil explicitly and the estimate says `.notSelfChecked`" — sees the probe radius threaded live from four call sites, and records that a shell radius implausibly small relative to the probe is caught and reported. Nothing catches it: an estimate built from a first shell sitting inside the probe disk returns `.measured` or `.notSelfChecked` on purely second-shell grounds, and the resulting `invAngstromPerPixel` is stamped `.measuredInApp` with the reader believing a probe-relative sanity check passed.

findings.title: `probeSize` uses `sorted[n/2]` where py4DSTEM uses `np.median`, an unmarked deviation in a file whose header promises every deviation is marked
findings.why: REFUTER NOTE — checked line by line and it stands exactly as written. `OriginCalibration.swift:54-55` is `let sorted = dr.sorted(); let median = sorted[n / 2]` with default `n = 100` (`:35`), i.e. the 51st order statistic; `References/py4DSTEM-dev/py4DSTEM/process/calibration/probe.py:54` is `mask = (dr_dtheta <= 0) * (dr_dtheta >= 2 * np.median(dr_dtheta))`, and `np.median` averages the 50th and 51st for even N. The rest of the port is faithful (the one-sided end gradients at `:49-51` match `np.gradient`). The file header at `:10-11` promises deviations are marked, and the file does mark two (`:62` and `:169`) — so the omission is an inconsistency within the file, not a missing convention. `docs/open-items.md` has no entry for it: the two live `probeSize` items (`:354-364` and `:585-600`) are about the max-DP counting Bragg disks as probe area (2.15× over-measure, Gate D owed), a different and much larger defect in the same function. Severity correctly stated as low: the discrepancy is bounded by half the gap between two adjacent order statistics of a 100-point gradient, and in the flat-plateau case where several `dr` values are exactly 0 the two definitions coincide. It is reportable because it is an unmarked deviation on a parity-checked path, not because the number moves much.
findings.failureScenario: On a pattern whose `dr(thresh)` has no exactly-flat plateau — the normal case, since the masked area changes by a few pixels at every threshold — `sorted[49] != sorted[50]`, so the acceptance bound `2 * median` at `:59` differs from py4DSTEM's and borderline threshold indices flip in or out of `trusted`. Both `r` (mean of `rVals[trusted]`, `:67`) and `thresh` (`:68`, which sets the CoM mask and hence x0/y0) then differ from `get_probe_size` on identical input, and the radius propagates into the CoM window, `DiskDetectionParams` peak spacing and the probe kernel scale. Any harness comparing the app's probe radius against py4DSTEM's — e.g. `tools/real-data-acceptance/main.swift:111` — is comparing two different estimators without saying so.

codeReview.area: Refutation pass over the AppState.swift (5416-line facade) review — five reported findings
codeReview.summary: I tried to kill all five and killed none: every cited line says what the reviewer claimed, and in each case I looked for the upstream guard, the documented decision, or the open-items entry that would refute it and did not find one. Two of the five are strengthened by evidence the reviewer did not cite (the `restoredResultPixelInfo` doc comment at AppState.swift:260-261 asserts a clearing that the code never performs — a docs-vs-code defect in its own right; and `setManualAcceleratingVoltage` DOES invalidate the ACOM *result* for mrad scales at AppState.swift:3215-3217, proving the voltage→ACOM coupling was considered and the plan half was missed). What is genuinely good here: the invalidation discipline around the origin is otherwise dense and commented with the Gate B findings that produced it (AppState.swift:3103-3117), the DPC publish path refuses to stamp "✓" over a failed derivation (AppState.swift:4310-4320), and S13's single `Calibration.referenceOrigin` derivation (Calibration.swift:652-676) really did close the four sites the S11 open item catalogued — the overlay finding is a fifth site that catalogue never named. I made three corrections: one wrong line number in finding 2, a narrower-than-claimed UI path for the same finding, and a mitigation the reviewer missed in finding 3 (a working Cancel remains in the Analysis menu), for which I lowered the severity from high to medium.

findings.title: restoredResultPixelInfo is never cleared, so a freshly computed product exports with the restored session map's pixel size, units and provenance
findings.why: CHECKED AND CONFIRMED. `grep -rn restoredResultPixelInfo --include='*.swift'` over the whole tree returns exactly eight hits: the declaration (AppState.swift:263), four assignment sites (AppState.swift:2950, :2962; ResultExport.swift:840, :852) and three reads (ResultExport.swift:723, :959, :1699). There is no `restoredResultPixelInfo = nil` anywhere. Its partner `restoredResultInfo` is nil-ed at 20 sites (AppState.swift:789, 2562, 3009, 3469, 3548, 3630, 3659, 3734, 3938, 3984, 4379, 4741, 4939, 4970, 5281; ResultExport.swift:1067). The consumer asymmetry is real: `currentResultKind/DisplayName/ValueUnits` (ResultExport.swift:1686-1695) key on `restoredResultInfo`, while `currentResultPersistenceMetadata` (ResultExport.swift:1698-1711) begins `restoredResultPixelInfo ?? navigationResultPixelInfo ?? currentScalarPersistenceMetadata` with no reference to `restoredResultInfo` — so a stale tuple wins unconditionally and also shadows the navigation tuple that `changeMode` (AppState.swift:1355-1362) sets. Consumers verified: ResultExport.swift:204-211 takes `pixel.row/column/units` for the burned-in scale bar, :232-240 writes `pixel.provenance` into the PNG metadata record, and AppState.swift:681-688 reads `sampling`/`quantitative_status` for `displayedProduct`. The intended pairing is proved twice — `saveCurrentResultToSessionSidecar` guards on `if restoredResultInfo != nil` before reading the pixel tuple (ResultExport.swift:722-724), and `selectedSavedControlRehydration` requires both non-nil (ResultExport.swift:959). ADDED EVIDENCE the reviewer did not cite: the declaration's own doc comment at AppState.swift:260-261 says "Set only while `resultImage` is the scalar map restored from the stable session sidecar. New scientific results clear it at publication" — a claim the code does not support for this field, so this is also a docs-vs-code defect. Cross-dataset leak confirmed: `activate` clears `restoredResultInfo` (:2562) and `comField` (:2579) but not the pixel tuple. Searched `docs/open-items.md` for pixel-size/scale-bar/persistence entries — not recorded. `grep` over `mac4DSTEMTests/` and `tools/` for either field returns nothing, so no test can catch it. Not refuted; severity high stands (a wrong burned-in scale bar is a quantitative claim the app is not entitled to make).
findings.failureScenario: Open a dataset whose sidecar holds a saved ptychography-phase map (pixelSizeRow = object sampling in Å, units "A"). `restoreSessionResult` (AppState.swift:2946-2971), reached from `activate` before the open's own analysis, sets both restored tuples. `openFileAsync` then runs its first whole-cube pass (`await runCurrentAnalysis()`, :2316) into `runVirtualDetector`, which sets `restoredResultInfo = nil` (:3938) and publishes a new scan-domain image. Title and units correctly read "Virtual detector", but `currentResultPersistenceMetadata` still returns the ptychography map's row/column/units/provenance. Export as a publication PNG: the burned-in scale bar is drawn at the object sampling in Å instead of the scan pixel size (ResultExport.swift:204-211), and the PNG metadata carries the ptychography `source_product` and `quantitative_status` (ResultExport.swift:232-240), which `displayedProduct` also inherits as the new product's trust badge.

findings.title: Changing the accelerating voltage does not invalidate the cached orientation plan, so ACOM re-runs against a flat-Ewald template library and reports in-plane angle only modulo 180°
findings.why: CHECKED AND CONFIRMED, with two corrections. `generateOrientationPlan` derives `planWavelength` from `acceleratingVoltage` (AppState.swift:5118-5124) and passes it to `OrientationPlan.generate`; the plan does NOT store the wavelength (`grep wavelength Core/Crystal/OrientationPlan.swift` returns only the parameter at :95, :122, :173 and its use at :184 — no stored property), so no downstream mismatch check is even possible. The physics claim is the repo's own: OrientationPlan.swift:153-159 states that without a wavelength every template is EXACTLY π-periodic in azimuth and the in-plane angle is determined only modulo 180°, and :184-185 implements `sg = g·n + (λ/2)|g|²`. `invalidateACOMPlan()` (:773-777) is called only from `acomModelSelection` (:443), `acomQuality` (:460), `customZ` (:765), `customStructure` (:767), `customLatticeA` (:770), and the plan is otherwise cleared only in `activate` (:2598). `setManualAcceleratingVoltage` (:3211-3218) clears the parallax products and calls `invalidateACOMResult()` — the result, not the plan — and only when `qPixelUnits` normalises to "mrad". `runACOM` regenerates only on absence: `if orientationPlan == nil { await generateOrientationPlan() }` (:5168). CORRECTION 1: the nil-set of `acceleratingVoltage` on a file with no metadata voltage is AppState.swift:2436, not :2477 (:2434 is the kV/V normalisation); both are inside `activate`, which clears the plan at :2598, so the file-metadata path is safe and only the manual setter leaks. CORRECTION 2: the voltage field is not a general inspector field — UI/ContentView.swift:505-518 renders it only under `workspaceArea == .reconstruct && analysisMode == .ptychography`, so the reachable sequence is: run ACOM with no voltage (plan built flat), go to Reconstruct/Ptychography, type the voltage, return to ACOM, re-run. Nothing clears the plan across those mode switches, so the stale library is reused. STRENGTHENING EVIDENCE: the mrad branch at :3215-3217 shows the author did consider voltage→ACOM coupling and handled only the scale half. Searched `docs/open-items.md` for voltage/orientationPlan entries — the OrientationPlan items at :709, :1422-1466 are about weighting, projection frame and `intensityPower`, not plan staleness. Not refuted; severity high stands.
findings.failureScenario: Open a file whose metadata carries no `accelerating_voltage` (`acceleratingVoltage = nil`, AppState.swift:2436). Run ACOM: the plan is generated with `wavelengthAngstrom: nil` — flat Ewald sphere, π-degenerate templates (OrientationPlan.swift:184). Prepare's readiness lists voltage as an unmet requirement (`ProductWorkflow.swift:272`, `:331`), so the user enters it in the Reconstruct panel's Voltage field (ContentView.swift:511). Return to ACOM and re-run: `orientationPlan != nil` at :5168, so the flat-Ewald library is reused unchanged. The IPF·Z, in-plane angle and Euler φ₁/φ₂ maps are published with 180° ambiguities the physical plan would have broken, carry the physical-scale provenance from `acomScaleSemantics` (:871-889), are recorded into the replay recipe and exported. Nothing on screen distinguishes this from a correctly generated plan.

findings.title: Cancel during an open's first whole-cube pass stops nothing and its own message is immediately overwritten by advancing progress
findings.why: CHECKED AND CONFIRMED, severity lowered from high. `cancelDatasetLoad()` (AppState.swift:1206-1213) cancels only `datasetLoadCancellation`; it never touches `operationController`. The open's final `await runCurrentAnalysis()` (:2316, and the sibling copies at :1657 and :1758) reaches `runVirtualDetector`, which mints its own token via `beginCancellableOperation` (:3390-3396) and hands only that token to `VirtualDetector.tiledRun`/`tiledImage` (:3434-3460) — `datasetLoadCancellation` is not consulted anywhere in that function. The message overwrite is real: `updateCancellableOperation` guards on `!token.isCancelled` for the ANALYSIS token (:1258) and then unconditionally does `if isLoadingDataset { datasetLoadingProgress = progress; datasetLoadingStatus = status }` (:1264-1268); neither it nor `reportDatasetLoadingProgress` consults `isCancellingDatasetLoad`. The button then disappears because `canCancelDatasetLoad` requires `!isCancellingDatasetLoad` (:1201-1203). I checked the UI to see whether a working Cancel is also on screen: `ProductWorkspaceHeader`, which hosts the `operationProgress` Cancel wired to `cancelActiveOperation` (UI/ProductWorkspaceViews.swift:327-329, :436-438), is rendered only under `hasDataset && !isLoadingDataset` (UI/ContentView.swift:974-975), so it is hidden during this phase; the welcome card's Cancel (ProductWorkspaceViews.swift:191-195) is the only one visible, exactly as claimed. MITIGATION THE REVIEWER MISSED, and the reason I lowered severity: the Analysis menu's "Cancel Analysis" (App/mac4DSTEMApp.swift:103-105, ⎋) calls `cancelActiveOperation` and is enabled throughout, so a knowledgeable user can stop the pass. Nothing is mis-computed and nothing is kept — `openFileAsync` observes `datasetLoadWasCancelled` at :2317 and discards — the cost is the full read of the cube and a visibly ignored control. `docs/open-items.md:812-824` records two other hazards of this same tail (a cancel swallowed between the last check and `finishDatasetLoading`; a second initiator replacing the shared token) and `:1872-1876` records that F1.1d has never been driven, but neither describes this one, so it is new. Not refuted.
findings.failureScenario: Open a 17 GB DM4 by mistake — the case the Cancel affordance was built for (its rationale is at AppState.swift:1190-1195). Metadata, preview (`buildDatasetPreview`, :2691-2703) and preload (`preloadResidentCube`, :2721-2737) all honour `datasetLoadCancellation`. The whole-cube virtual-detector pass then starts and the card shows "Scanning patterns 1,378 / 16,218 · …". Press Cancel: `isCancellingDatasetLoad` goes true, the button vanishes (:1201-1203), "Cancelling…" shows for one frame and is then replaced by the next progress tick (:1264-1268), and the counter climbs to 16,218 while the entire cube is read. Only afterwards does :2317 observe the flag and discard to the welcome screen. The user sees a Cancel that was visibly ignored, with no way to press it again and no indication that the menu item would have worked.

findings.title: The cached CoM field is not invalidated when the origin it was measured against changes, so a later DPC display switch renders it under the new origin's provenance
findings.why: CHECKED AND CONFIRMED. `grep -n comField AppState.swift` returns exactly four lines: the declaration (:348), the only clear (`activate`, :2579), the only write (`runDPC`, :4308) and the only read (`applyDPCDisplay`, :4378). The cache's defining input is confirmed at :4222-4227 — `computeCoMField` passes `calibration.origin?.interleavedFitted` as `origins` and `calibration.referenceOrigin(...).point` as `center` into `VirtualDetector.tiledCenterOfMass`. Both mutators of that input leave the cache alone while clearing their neighbours: `updateAperture` (:3095-3125) moves the fitted maps to `supersededFittedOrigin`, sets `calibration.origin = nil`, clears `recordedOriginX/Y`, stamps `.manual` and clears `parallaxPreprocess`/`parallaxAlignment` (:3118-3119) but not `comField`; `restoreFittedOrigin` (:3080-3093) reinstates the maps, moves the aperture and again clears only the parallax pair. The contrast with `calibrateRotation`, which explicitly re-derives the display because "a cached CoM field must not show a stale rotation" (:4233-4240 comment, `applyDPCDisplay()` at :4241), is the strongest evidence this is an oversight rather than a decision — the same author closed the rotation half of exactly this hazard. `dpcDisplay`'s didSet calls `applyDPCDisplay()` (:973-975), which re-renders straight from the cache with no origin check, and `idpcPhysicalCalibration` (:4476-4498) admits physical iDPC on `hasFittedOrigin && hasRotation` plus the `gates.originQuantitativeRefusal` gate — all live state, none of it describing what was actually subtracted. Export provenance is likewise read from live calibration at export time (ResultExport.swift:1477-1522), including `"origins_subtracted": calibration.hasFittedOrigin ? "fitted_per_position" : "none"` (:1516-1517). I checked whether either mutator indirectly re-runs DPC: `scheduleLiveVirtualDetector` (:3120, :3092) returns immediately unless `analysisMode == .virtualDetector` (:3220), so it cannot. Nothing in `docs/open-items.md` records it. Not refuted; medium is the right level — reaching it needs a specific interactive sequence, but the output is a radians-labelled quantitative map.
findings.failureScenario: In Virtual Detector mode drag the aperture centre: `updateAperture` supersedes the fitted maps and stamps `.manual` (:3103-3117). Switch to DPC and run it — `comField` is now measured about that single manual centre with `origins = nil`, i.e. no per-position origins subtracted (:4222-4227). Go to Prepare and press Restore Fitted Origin (:3080): the maps return, `hasFittedOrigin` is true again, `comField` is untouched. Back in DPC, change the display to iDPC: `applyDPCDisplay` (:4378) renders from the stale cache, and because `idpcPhysicalCalibration` now passes, the image is integrated as PHYSICAL iDPC in radians (:4415-4420). Exporting it writes `"quantitative": "true"` and the fitted-origin sampling (ResultExport.swift:1478-1495) for a field whose per-position origins were never subtracted.

findings.title: The strain and ACOM fit-verification overlays are anchored on a fifth hand-rolled origin fallback, so they are drawn at a different point than the analysis they verify
findings.why: CHECKED AND CONFIRMED. `overlayReferenceOrigin` reads `calibration.meanOrigin ?? (x: Float(d.qx)/2, y: Float(d.qy)/2)` (AppState.swift:5310-5313) and is the only origin passed to `strainFitOverlay` (:5333) and `acomFitOverlay` (:5350). The analyses those overlays verify go through `calibratedBraggVectors` (:4752-4770), whose in-code comment records that this exact expression — `calibration.meanOrigin ?? (qx/2, qy/2)` — was what S13 replaced there, and which now calls `calibration.referenceOrigin(...)`. That function's doc comment is explicit: "**The one derivation of 'which origin do I re-centre on?'**" and "A new caller belongs here, not in a fifth hand-rolled `?? (qx/2, qy/2)`" (Core/Data/Calibration.swift:652-659); its order is fittedMaps → recordedMean → apertureCentre → geometricMiddle (:661-677). The two therefore agree only in the `.fittedMaps` state and disagree whenever `calibration.origin` is nil but a beam centre is known. I checked whether the difference is absorbed downstream and it is not: `FitOverlays.localOrigin` returns the passed `referenceOrigin` unchanged under exactly the same map-usability rule (Core/Analysis/FitOverlays.swift:64-79), and `rawPoint` then builds every marker and vector from it (:81-91). The magnitude is this repo's own measurement of the same substitution: 1.14 px on `sim_Au`, 7.07 px on `downsample_Si_SiGe_exp` (Calibration.swift:598-601, and `docs/open-items.md:395-400`). Checked open-items before agreeing this is new: the S11 entry (`docs/open-items.md:404-424`) enumerates the affected sites as `calibratedBraggVectors`, Q calibration, strain, ACOM, the Bragg map, plus three siblings (`computeCoMField`, `generateMeasuredProbeKernel`, `calibrateEllipse`) — the fit overlays appear nowhere in that catalogue, and the entry is marked closed structurally by S13. So this site survived the fix that was supposed to be structural. Not refuted; medium is right — it corrupts a human judgement instrument rather than an exported number.
findings.failureScenario: Open a py4DSTEM bundle carrying `qx0_mean`/`qy0_mean` with no per-position origin maps — the ordinary shape of a calibration bundle (Calibration.swift:626-628; `H5Reader` reads the means unconditionally and the maps only if present, per `docs/open-items.md:418-420`). `activate` stores them as `recordedOriginX/Y`, leaving `calibration.origin` nil, so `meanOrigin` is nil and `referenceOrigin` returns kind `.recordedMean`. Run disk detection then strain: the map is computed about the recorded beam centre. Turn on the fit overlay and inspect a position: `overlayReferenceOrigin` (:5311) falls to `(qx/2, qy/2)` instead, so the reference and local lattice vectors are drawn from a point up to 7.07 px away on that dataset, systematically offset from the stored raw peaks (`storedPeaksAtSelection`, :5318) they are meant to be judged against. The user reads a correct fit as bad — or accepts a bad one — from the instrument built to make that judgement.
